subject: history
title: Gandhi, Quit India and Partition 1947
welcome_lead: Follow Gandhi's non-violent campaigns, the Quit India movement and the catastrophic partition of 1947.
meta_desc: A-Level adventure on Indian independence: satyagraha, Quit India 1942, Mountbatten's plan and Partition 1947.
final_note: You can analyse why partition accompanied freedom and at what human cost.

concepts.def: Gandhi's doctrine of 'truth-force' non-violent civil disobedience, first developed in South Africa and applied in India from 1917.
240-mile march to Dandi to make salt in defiance of the British monopoly, launching the Civil Disobedience movement.
Major statute granting provincial autonomy and envisaging an all-India federation; basis of Congress ministries 1937.
Mass movement launched by Congress on 8 August 1942 demanding immediate British withdrawal; leaders were imprisoned.
Last Viceroy's 3 June 1947 plan to partition British India into India and Pakistan, with independence on 15 August 1947.
Division of British India along the Radcliffe Line, causing mass migration of an estimated 10-15 million people and up to 1 million deaths in communal violence.

walkthroughs.body_html: Gandhi transformed Congress into a mass movement. The Non-Cooperation movement (1920-22) followed Amritsar; the Salt March (March-April 1930) dramatised tax injustice. The Round Table Conferences (1930-32) and Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931) failed to deliver dominion status. The 1935 Act produced Congress provincial ministries in 1937 but excluded the centre.

Viceroy Linlithgow declared war on Germany without consulting Indian leaders, prompting Congress ministries to resign in 1939. The Cripps Mission (1942) offered post-war dominion status; Gandhi called it 'a post-dated cheque'. The Quit India resolution (8 August 1942) triggered the Bombay 'Do or Die' speech and mass arrests. Subhas Chandra Bose led the Indian National Army alongside Japan.

The 1946 Cabinet Mission failed to secure agreement on a federal solution. Direct Action Day (16 August 1946) saw the Great Calcutta Killings. Viceroy Mountbatten accelerated the timetable: the 3 June 1947 Plan announced partition, and the Indian Independence Act received Royal Assent on 18 July 1947. Cyril Radcliffe drew the boundary lines in five weeks. Independence came at midnight on 15 August 1947, accompanied by horrific communal violence in Punjab and Bengal.

mcqs.q: Why did the British Empire end after WWII?
options: The UN forced Britain to grant independence to all colonies in 1945.
Britain voluntarily gave its colonies independence as a moral choice.
Gandhi insisted on partition to ensure Hindu dominance.
Britain was bankrupted by the war, faced rising nationalist movements, and confronted US/Soviet pressure against colonialism in a new world order.
The UN forced Britain to grant independence to all colonies in 1945.
Hindus and Muslims had always hated each other so partition was inevitable.
Gandhi insisted on partition to ensure Hindu dominance.
The Muslim League's demand for Pakistan, Congress refusal of power-sharing, communal violence, British haste to leave, and Mountbatten's accelerated timetable.
